clue.text: Horse making painful sound, not good

indicators.note: 'not good' tells us the letter for good is dropped from the sound

parts.note: a groan is a sound of pain

explanation.surface: A horse is whinnying in pain, which is not a good sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs is so called; the word names the animal itself.

clue.text: Holy objects kept outside bar in places like Ireland

indicators.note: the holy objects are kept around the bar

parts.note: relics are sacred objects venerated by believers
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: Sacred items stored outside a pub in Irish places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept outside' looks like it describes the relics' storage, but it says the holy objects wrap round the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a state with an elected head and no monarch; an example of the kind.

clue.text: Optical problem, as designers then worked out

indicators.note: the letters are worked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Designers diagnosed an eye condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges AS DESIGNERS THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia, being unable to see distant things clearly, is a vision defect.

clue.text: They look back at Irish son undergoing transformation

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are being transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: People stare at an Irish lad who is going through a big change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing transformation' rearranges the ten letters of AT IRISH SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars of the past study earlier times, so they figuratively look back.

clue.text: Cook fowl as a pagan

parts.note: to heat food is to cook it
a hen is a domestic fowl

explanation.surface: A pagan cooks a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone outside the main religions, a nonbeliever.

clue.text: Nameless tough fighters arising to be rulers

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means the remaining letters read upwards
name abbreviates to N, so the fighters lose that letter

parts.note: Spartans were the famously hardy warriors of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: Anonymous hard soldiers rise up to take power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N from SPARTANS to leave SPARTAS; 'arising' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Provincial governors of ancient Persia; the word is now used for any petty tyrants.

clue.text: Old writer having drink becomes more communicative

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An elderly author takes a drink and grows chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to talk freely and frankly; becoming forthcoming is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Imprisoned frequently, I am free finally — just before something terrible happens?

parts.note: in the nick is British slang for in prison
oft is an old word for often
I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word free is used

explanation.surface: A convict, often jailed, finally declares freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E from free. 'Nick' is British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning at the last possible moment, before disaster arrives.

clue.text: Not happy eating the French food with few calories

indicators.note: the unhappy word takes in, eats, the French article

parts.note: sad means unhappy
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A miserable dieter eats light French fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' means taking in: the French article goes inside the word for unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy raw vegetables are a typical low-calorie dish, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Nice line penned by country person

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the line sits inside the country person

parts.note: a peasant is a rural worker

explanation.surface: A rustic writes a kind line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts L inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and agreeable are synonyms describing something enjoyable.

clue.text: Mean chaps heading off with dog

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for chaps is cut away

parts.note: chaps are men
to dog someone is to follow, or tail, them

explanation.surface: Some men set off with their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes M from MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean a consequence is to involve or necessitate it, a verb sense these share.

clue.text: Soup served in club or school

indicators.note: the letters are dished up inside the run of words club or school

explanation.surface: A soup is on the menu at a club or a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' signals letters inside clu(B OR SCH)ool.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetroot broth from Eastern Europe, one spelling among several.

clue.text: Satisfied raw needs somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Basic needs were met in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RAW NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or demand is to respond to it, so satisfied a requirement equals responded to it.

clue.text: One reigning over a period

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second; that the three letters also run on through 'over a' is a coincidence

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a reigning queen
taken as written; its run with 'over' is a coincidence, not the device

explanation.surface: A monarch ruling for a span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch of history is a period.

clue.text: Pictures of wise men entering home, leaders of esoteric society

indicators.note: the wise men go into the word for home

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the Magi are the wise men of the nativity story

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Images of the three wise men arriving at the headquarters of a secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' reads as a noun but is the verb; 'entering' and 'leaders of' are the two indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to envision it in the mind, a verb sense these share.

clue.text: Original friend across the border

indicators.note: the friend stretches across, around, the border

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A first-time friend from over the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the border' suggests a foreign friend, but 'across' means the friend spans the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something primeval or first in time is primary, the earliest form.

clue.text: Member is no longer with us — make provision in law

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written
late means dead

explanation.surface: An MP has died, so the law must provide for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass laws is the work of a parliament, enacting provision by statute.

clue.text: Announces conditions

definitions.meaning: situations or circumstances one is in

explanation.surface: Someone announces the terms.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb meaning declares and a plural noun for situations.

clue.text: Article subsequently shortened

indicators.note: the word for subsequently loses its last letter

parts.note: then means afterwards

explanation.surface: A piece of writing was later cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' removes the final N from THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The definite article in English grammar.

clue.text: Remove handicap for excellent golfer

definitions.meaning: to withdraw an entrant from a race
a zero handicap, the mark of a top amateur golfer

explanation.surface: A top golfer's handicap is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for withdrawing a competitor, and the golf term for a handicap of zero.

clue.text: Excellent solving

definitions.meaning: working out a code or problem, as one breaks a cipher

explanation.surface: A solver congratulated on doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang adjective for first-rate, and the participle of breaking a code.

clue.text: Makes fusses

definitions.meaning: in British informal use, to make a fuss or complain

explanation.surface: Someone causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to produce and, in British slang, to kick up a fuss.

clue.text: Gives a couple of females commands, no hesitation

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them

indicators.note: no hesitation means the hesitation sound is taken out

parts.note: orders are commands
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone gives two women orders without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ER from ORDERS to leave ODS.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide or supply something, a verb sense these share.

clue.text: Policeman supplying information to lady outside front of restaurant

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the lady goes around the letter that follows

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady

indicators.note: the first letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: An officer passes a tip to a woman outside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts R inside DAME; 'front of' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A French armed officer of the law is the term borrowed here.

clue.text: Dance with girl before work

indicators.note: the girl comes before the work

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A girl goes dancing before heading to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 19th-century ballroom dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Players from part of Scotland — odd characters from Ross

parts.note: Fife is a region of eastern Scotland

indicators.note: the first and third letters of Ross

explanation.surface: Musicians from a Scottish region including some eccentrics from Ross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters from' takes R and S from Ross; Ross is also a Scottish area, adding to the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of the small flute in a band are musicians, so players fits.

clue.text: Previous set of books undiscovered

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An old collection of books has never been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden or dormant, present but not yet revealed, so undiscovered.

clue.text: Run around unwell, having taken a piece of food

indicators.note: the word for run is turned round

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A runner feels sick after eating something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals turning the word for run backwards; 'having taken' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat Mexican bread, or a Spanish omelette, is an item one eats.

clue.text: What Paralympian may have — he is involved with sports

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are entangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A Paralympic athlete is described taking part in sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes HE IS and SPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Many disabled athletes use an artificial limb, the example the definition hints at.

clue.text: River coming into hovel below

indicators.note: the letters come into view inside the words hovel below

explanation.surface: A river floods a shack beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming into' signals letters inside hov(EL BE)low.
explanation.definitionFit: A major waterway of central Europe, flowing through Germany to the North Sea.
